topic: Cheaper per-lane isolation than full git worktrees: sparse or partial checkouts, shallow and reference clones, overlay or copy-on-write filesystems, single worktree with per-lane write redirection, per-lane sandboxed working directories with a shared object store, and one-checkout exact-attribution variants

noveltyJustification: First evidence pass; repo anatomy and mechanism-to-surface mapping are new

ruledOut.reason: truncates history not tree; full 1.4 GB materialization remains; new repo boundary breaks sweep machinery
object sharing is already free under one repo; documented corruption hazard when source is pruned
promisor fetches couple lane liveness to source location; breaks churn detector on relocation

focus: non-git mechanisms vs the attribution invariant
noveltyJustification: Attribution invariant, detector hard-fail vs fail-open split, and wrong-tree recreation are new; redirection restates a scored 3/10 decision

ruledOut.reason: lane is not a git working tree: detector hard-fails or fails open, sweep cannot reclaim, git index coherence breaks

ruledOut.approach: single worktree with per-lane write redirection
ruledOut.reason: already scored 3/10 in ADR-003; executor levers make redirection a project, and ADR-005 watch is report-only

ruledOut.approach: per-lane sandboxed dir with shared object store
ruledOut.reason: without a git identity the store is unreachable and the detector is blind; with one it is a clone or a worktree
runner status calls use the repo default index, so the detector watches the shared checkout while the lane writes its own tree

focus: frontier comparison, relocation matrix, adoption path, web verification
noveltyJustification: Cost table, relocation matrix and adoption path are new; git-behavior claims upgraded from hypothesis to cited fact
